&l;!–donotpaginate–&g;&l;p&g;Proponents of the Obama-era fiduciary rule, meant to protect retirement investors and put on hold by President Donald Trump, are back in court, fighting for its life. Their entry into the fray yesterday comes after a three-judge panel of the 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit overturned the Department of Labor rule in March in a case brought by the U.S. Chamber of Commerce of the U.S. against the DOL. The AARP and three state Attorneys General&a;mdash;New York&a;rsquo;s Eric Schneiderman, California&a;rsquo;s Xavier Becerra and Oregon&a;rsquo;s Ellen Rosenblum&a;mdash;are asking the 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit to rehear the case en banc (the AARP&s;s filing is &l;a href=&q;https://www.aarp.org/content/dam/aarp/politics/advocacy/2018/04/final-petition-for-rehearing-appendix-chamber-v-dol.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;here&l;/a&g;; the AGs&s; filings are &l;a href=&q;https://ag.ny.gov/sites/default/files/motion_to_intervene_filed.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;here&l;/a&g; and &l;a href=&q;https://ag.ny.gov/sites/default/files/en_banc_filed.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;here&l;/a&g;).
&a;ldquo;The concern is that the DOL is potentially either not going to appeal or not going to aggressively defend the fiduciary rule,&a;rdquo; says Erin Sweeney, an employee benefits lawyer with Miller &a;amp; Chevalier in Washington, D.C. &a;ldquo;Part of this could be the states and AARP&a;rsquo;s opening volley: We&a;rsquo;re going to fight this to the death.&a;rsquo;&a;rdquo;
&l;img class=&q;dam-image shutterstock size-large wp-image-1078171904&q; src=&q;https://specials-images.forbesimg.com/dam/imageserve/1078171904/960×0.jpg?fit=scale&q; data-height=&q;640&q; data-width=&q;960&q;&g; Shutterstock
The DOL has until April 30 to file for en banc review before the 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit, or June 14 to appeal directly to the U.S. Supreme Court.
In taking up the old DOL position, AARP argues that invalidating the fiduciary rule and exemptions will jeopardize the retirement security of millions of Americans. And the Attorneys General argue that their residents stand to lose billions of dollars in investment gains if the rule is invalidated.
Under the fiduciary rule, any advisor getting paid to provide individualized retirement advice (what assets to purchase or sell, or whether to roll over a 401(k) plan balance into an Individual Retirement Account, for example), would be a fiduciary and have to put clients&a;rsquo; interests first.
The DOL fiduciary rule has had a tortured path. It was first proposed in 2010, then a revised version came out in 2016, only to immediately face scrutiny and legal challenges from industry players including the Insured Retirement Institute and the Securities Industry and Financial Markets Association. After President Trump ordered the DOL to review the rule in February 2017, the DOL said it wouldn&a;rsquo;t enforce the rule in the near term, so the rule officially kicked in last June, with no bite.
The 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit decision in favor of the Chamber of Commerce was a 2-1 split decision, rejecting the DOL&a;rsquo;s argument that the common law meaning of &a;ldquo;fiduciary&a;rdquo;&a;mdash;which the court said doesn&a;rsquo;t extend to broker-dealers, insurance agents or other sales people–should be displaced by the new rule.
Now, the question is whether the 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit will agree to review the case. The make-up of the 5&l;sup&g;th&l;/sup&g; Circuit is by and large Republican appointees. &a;ldquo;It&a;rsquo;s hard to see how a majority votes in favor of en banc review,&a;rdquo; Sweeney says.
In the meantime, the SEC has proposed its own lower standards for all investment advice–suitability-plus&a;mdash;that&a;rsquo;s designed to make sure the advisors&a;rsquo; interests aren&a;rsquo;t put ahead of the investors&a;rsquo; interests, not so much that you&a;rsquo;re looking out for the best interest of the investors. The SEC action makes it less likely that the Supreme Court will take this case, Sweeney says, because the Chamber would likely argue in an opposing petition for cert that now that the SEC is actively engaged on the topic, there&a;rsquo;s a lot more development on the record that should take place. (Here are links to the SEC&s;s three proposals on &l;a href=&q;https://www.sec.gov/rules/proposed/2018/34-83063.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;relationship summaries&l;/a&g;, &l;a href=&q;https://www.sec.gov/rules/proposed/2018/ia-4889.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;new standards of conduct&l;/a&g;, and &l;a href=&q;https://www.sec.gov/rules/proposed/2018/34-83062.pdf&q; target=&q;_blank&q;&g;best interest regulation&l;/a&g;).
So, what happens next to retirement assets? Who is going to be the author of the standard and what standard is going to apply? &q;That&s;s the gazillion dollar question,&q; Sweeney says.&l;/p&g; This entry was posted in Best Stocks on by admin . Post navigation
